decision.detail: He crosses the lobby floor without looking up at the chandeliers, though the light hits the glass housing of the reel in his left hand and he turns it once, slow, between his fingers, reading the tag he wrote in the booth: ALMA / RIALTO / 1 TAKE / L. He sets it on the station counter, flat, label up, next to the patch port where Rita's copy already sits in its sleeve. He peels the second tag off the roll—PITTS / THURS / REGIONAL LINE—and presses it to the reel with his thumb. He does not pick it up again. He pushes it two inches toward the counter edge so it's in the handoff zone. Then he pulls his coat collar up, turns, and walks toward the door without waiting for a receipt or a nod.
decision.intention: Get the reel onto the regional line before the last train. Pittsburgh by Thursday, earlier if the switch in Altoona runs clean. The shot is done. The job is to move the object. Everything else—the lights, the piano, the party—is somebody else's evening.
decision.words: Nothing to Rita. Nothing to the room. Just the small sound of the reel's plastic sliding on the laminate, and his own breathing, and the station line humming under the floor.
